Add the PHW Quarto extension to a project

Source: R/quarto.R
use_phw_quarto.Rd

Copies the phw Quarto extension into _extensions/phw inside path. This is the same as running quarto add, but it works offline. You can also write a starter document.

Usage

use_phw_quarto(
  path = ".",
  template = c("report", "slides", "dashboard", "none"),
  overwrite = FALSE
)

Arguments

path

Project folder.

template

Also write a starter document: "report", "slides", "dashboard", or "none".

overwrite

Replace an existing extension or template?

Value

The extension path, invisibly.

Details

The extension provides these formats:

FormatOutput
phw-htmlWeb report with the gradient header band and logo
phw-docxWord report built from the PHW reference document
phw-pptxPowerPoint slides built from the PHW template
phw-typstPDF via Typst (fast, no LaTeX needed) with cover and band
phw-pdfPDF via XeLaTeX with cover and band
phw-revealjs16:9 slides with gradient title slide, logo and footer
phw-dashboardQuarto dashboard with gradient navbar and PHW cards

Use them in the document's YAML:

format:
  phw-html: default
  phw-docx: default
  phw-typst: default

Typst options: phw-team: "Communicable Disease Surveillance Centre" adds a team line to the cover, and phw-no-cover: true drops the cover. phw-org, phw-page-label and phw-of-label change the footer wording ("Public Health Wales", "Page", "of").

The extension styles the document. The charts and tables your R code makes are styled by phwstyle itself, so call use_phw_ggplot() (and use_phw_flextable() for flextable) once in the setup chunk, as the starter documents do.

Accessible colours. Add phw-palette: accessible to the document's YAML header and every chart, table and widget made with phwstyle uses the colour-blind safe palette:

title: "Report title"
phw-palette: accessible
format: phw-docx

To make both versions from one unchanged document, set the environment variable PHWSTYLE_PALETTE for the second render instead:

quarto render report.qmd --to phw-docx
PHWSTYLE_PALETTE=accessible quarto render report.qmd --to phw-docx -o report-accessible.docx

In PowerShell, set it first with $env:PHWSTYLE_PALETTE = "accessible" (and clear it afterwards with Remove-Item Env:PHWSTYLE_PALETTE). From R, use Sys.setenv(PHWSTYLE_PALETTE = "accessible") before rendering and Sys.unsetenv("PHWSTYLE_PALETTE") after. The key has to be in the document itself: Quarto doesn't pass -M values or _quarto.yml settings on to R. See phw_default_palette().

Examples

project <- file.path(tempdir(), "phw-quarto-example")
use_phw_quarto(project, template = "report")
#> ✔ Added the PHW Quarto extension to
#>   /tmp/RtmpYgLnk6/phw-quarto-example/_extensions/phw.
#> ℹ No PHW logo found, so outputs won't show one. See `phw_download_logos()`.
#> ✔ Wrote /tmp/RtmpYgLnk6/phw-quarto-example/report.qmd.
list.files(project)
#> [1] "_extensions" "report.qmd" 
# Then render report.qmd with Quarto, e.g. the Render button in RStudio.
unlink(project, recursive = TRUE)
